Local fork of github.com/markusmobius/go-dateparser v1.4.7.

The application uses Go 1.26. The optional upstream toolchain go1.27.1
preference is removed. Keep the upstream source, generator and BSD-3-Clause
license.

The 205 generated locale constructors retain their original bodies and build
their regional variants together. zz-lazy.go maps the language name to its
constructor. locale_cache.go uses the generated locale catalog to select one
family, publishes immutable values, and clears the constructor staging slots.
Construction is serialized. The eight most recently used locale values stay
resident. A live caller can obtain the same value again through a weak pointer.
The applicability dictionary is owned by the locale value.

The parser validates and orders all names before iterating them. A successful
parse stops further construction. A caller explicitly requesting the full list
receives all the values and owns its result slice. An unrecognized string can
still visit every language. That costs a cold scan, and the temporary values
are eligible for collection when the caller releases them.

When regenerating language tables, keep the renamed constructor entry points
and the generated switch for looking up each staging slot. Run the package
tests, the cold concurrent lookup and eviction tests, and the application
tracker date fixtures. Measurements on the NAS are in
docs/nas-memory-0.58.14-verification.md in the host project.
